questions.stem: A 59-year-old male patient presented with complaint of right sided facial weakness and loss of sensation on right side of the face with left side of body. Examination reveals Horner’s syndrome, nystagmus, vertigo, ataxia, hoarseness and dysphagia. The patient is not able to balance himself. What is the most common cause of this presentation?

options.label: A
options.text: Due to occlusion of the right posterior inferior cerebellar artery

options.label: B
options.text: Due to occlusion of the basilar artery

options.label: C
options.text: Due to occlusion of left posterior inferior cerebellar artery

options.label: D
options.text: Due to occlusion of anterior inferior cerebellar artery
